title: A phone secretly reports its owner's movements
mechanism_summary: An abusive person installs stalkerware without the device owner's knowledge. The software can reveal locations and private communications to the abuser.
suggested_beats: An abuser gains device access.
Private movements become known.
Seek safety support using a safer device.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone whose device may be monitored
why_it_works: Hidden surveillance can make the abuser appear impossible to escape.

title: A concealed microphone exposes private conversations
mechanism_summary: Stalkerware may activate a device microphone or capture phone conversations. An abusive person uses the access to monitor information never shared with them.
suggested_beats: A device is secretly monitored.
The abuser knows private conversations.
Plan safely before changing a monitored device.
why_it_works: Knowledge of private conversations can intimidate without revealing the surveillance tool.

title: A blocked contact follows across platforms
mechanism_summary: A person repeatedly pursues someone across different online accounts after contact is unwelcome. The persistent appearances communicate that the target cannot easily get away.
suggested_beats: Contact is unwelcome.
The same person appears on other platforms.
Document the pattern and report it.
why_it_works: Persistent pursuit can wear down boundaries and create a sense of inescapability.

title: Smart-home controls become a tool of intimidation
mechanism_summary: An abusive person remotely changes internet-connected devices in the target's home. Small unexplained changes can be used to frighten the person or undermine confidence in their perceptions.
suggested_beats: Home devices behave unexpectedly.
An abuser controls the changes remotely.
Seek support for a safe technology plan.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone sharing connected-home access with an abuser
why_it_works: Hard-to-explain changes can make a person doubt their own observations.

title: A supposed rescuer created the harassment
mechanism_summary: A person facing unwanted online contact receives help from someone who knows suspiciously much about it. The helper may be the person causing the abuse, seeking dependence and isolation.
suggested_beats: Unwanted contact creates distress.
An unusually informed helper offers rescue.
Seek independent support outside that relationship.
why_it_works: Manufactured danger can make its instigator appear indispensable.

title: Fake dating profiles recruit strangers into harassment
mechanism_summary: A cyberstalker created dating profiles using another person's photographs and contact information. Strangers then directed unwanted solicitations and messages toward that person.
suggested_beats: An impostor creates dating profiles.
Strangers begin contacting the target.
Report the profiles and preserve evidence.
why_it_works: A false profile makes outsiders believe the target invited their contact.

title: Unwanted registrations generate a flood of contact
mechanism_summary: A cyberstalker enrolled another person in numerous programs without consent. The resulting calls and emails turned legitimate services into instruments of harassment.
suggested_beats: A stalker submits unwanted registrations.
Unrelated services repeatedly contact the target.
Document the coordinated pattern and seek help.
why_it_works: Many apparently unrelated senders can make an organized attack hard to recognize.

title: New accounts evade an explicit block
mechanism_summary: A harasser makes replacement accounts to keep contacting someone who blocked them. The repeated evasion prolongs abuse beyond the target's attempt to end it.
suggested_beats: A target blocks an abusive account.
A replacement account resumes contact.
Report the repeated evasion as a pattern.
who_falls_for_it_archetype: someone trying to stop online harassment
why_it_works: Repeated boundary violations can make platform controls feel ineffective.
